title: Machine-learning screening identified experimentally active pore-forming peptides
summary: Machine-learning models and membrane-related filters were used to prioritize natural peptide sequences for testing. The study reports seven experimentally active peptides; three showed broad-spectrum activity and pore-forming evidence in the reported membrane assays. Peptide 615 had already been disclosed in a Peking University patent published in March 2025, before the related preprint and journal article. This entry represents one study campaign and makes no first-disclosure or sequence-novelty claim. Assay results do not establish clinical safety or efficacy.
ai_technology: ProtBERT-BFD sequence embeddings with a support-vector classifier and membrane-interaction, secondary-structure and contact-map predictions
organization: Peking University; Yantai University; Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne; University of Geneva; Songshan Lake Materials Laboratory

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full text, metadata and affiliation block; published patent text for earlier public disclosure; primary preprint record identified in the frozen source review.

evidence.tested: The paper reports seven experimentally active selected peptides and pore-forming measurements for three broad-spectrum candidates.
evidence.unknown: One peptide sequence, 615, was disclosed in an earlier university patent. The article does not establish clinical safety or efficacy, and no universal mechanism is claimed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning sequence and membrane-related models prioritized peptide candidates for experimental testing.
